panels.title: How far back these panels can see

options.content:
These panels are drawn from **Prometheus**, whose retention here is **15 days** (`docker-compose.yml`, `--storage.tsdb.retention.time=15d`). A gauge cannot be backfilled, so the left-hand side of every graph is empty for reasons that have nothing to do with the game.

**The authority is `daily_rollup` in `analytics.db`**, which keeps every day it has ever computed and can re-derive the rest from `daily_active` (180 days). For anything older than two weeks, query that table — design/21 §2.5 (A5).

panels.title: Daily active installs — total
panels.description: Distinct installs that sent at least one event on the last COMPLETE day (design/21 §2.4). An install is a browser, not a person and not an account: it is the id the game already stored for multiplayer, reused so that analytics adds no new identifier. Today is never included — a partial day's DAU is a number that keeps changing while looking like a measurement. **An absent line is not a zero.** This dashboard deliberately has no `or vector(0)` anywhere: the server omits a gauge it cannot answer, so a panel that says No data is saying we do not know yet, and a panel showing 0 is saying we measured zero. Those are different facts and the first week of a launch is full of the former.

panels.title: Daily active installs — by build target
panels.description: The same number split by where the player was: our own site, the WeChat mini-game, or a game portal. This is a PARTITION of the panel on the left — an install that played on two targets in one day is counted once, on whichever it appeared on first — so these lines sum to the total rather than overlapping it. If they ever do not, the cohort table's primary key has changed.

panels.title: Retention — D1 to D7
panels.description: For each offset N: of the installs active on some day, the share that were active again N days later. The cohort behind each line is the NEWEST one whose answer is known, which is `the last complete day minus N` — so the D7 line is about a cohort a week older than the D1 line, by construction. A missing line means no cohort has aged that far yet. **An absent line is not a zero.** This dashboard deliberately has no `or vector(0)` anywhere: the server omits a gauge it cannot answer, so a panel that says No data is saying we do not know yet, and a panel showing 0 is saying we measured zero. Those are different facts and the first week of a launch is full of the former.

panels.title: Cohort size behind each retention line
panels.description: How many installs the percentages on the left are computed over. Read this FIRST: a D1 of 50% over a cohort of 2 is one player coming back, and a launch-week dashboard is full of exactly that. Every rate is published with its denominator for this reason.

panels.title: Events per day, by name
panels.description: Every event stored on the last complete day, by name — the raw material of the funnel. The vocabulary is a closed list fixed in the game's code (`client/src/net/analyticsEvents.ts`), so a name that is NOT here is a name nothing sent, never a name the server rejected: anything off the list is dropped before it reaches a row.

panels.title: Funnel — did a visit reach a run, and finish one?
panels.description: The steps that matter on the last complete day, as counts: visits started, the forge reached, runs started, runs ended. Read as ratios rather than absolutes — `run_start / session_start` is how many visits reach a run at all, and `run_end / run_start` is how many runs are seen through. All are counts of EVENTS, not of installs, so a player who plays four runs contributes four.

panels.title: Screens reached, by screen
panels.description: Every `screen_view` on the last complete day, split by which screen. This is the early funnel in one panel: a visit that never leaves `menu` never reached the mode select, and a `store` count with no `store_purchase` beside it is the conversion question. Screen ids come from an explicit table in the client (`game/analyticsTracking.ts`) rather than from the phase names, because the server's id charset would refuse `modeSelect` and the step would silently never appear.

panels.title: Store — views against purchases
panels.description: The commercial conversion, such as it is while nothing is on sale: how many players opened the store, and how many bought. There is deliberately no `store_open` event — opening the store IS a screen view, and a second event for the same act would be two numbers to keep in agreement by hand.

panels.title: Rewarded ad — offered vs taken
panels.description: The one commercial number this instrumentation carries today (design/20's rewarded-ad offer). `ad_completed / ad_offer_shown` is the take-up rate of an offer the player has to accept — nothing plays unless they do, so a low rate is a product finding and not a bug.
